structured.approach: I read the four contracted inputs: feat.stories, feat.design, feat.clarifications and org.risk_map. I also used the code in the step's tool view. I gave each committed story one engineering task. STORY-01 to STORY-07 map to the approved design tasks DT-1 to DT-7, and the end-to-end story became TSK-08 for the Testing Agent. Each task has a goal, the design components it touches, its story acceptance criteria and pending markers, the tests to add (from feat.design B1.5 to B4.5 and feat.clarifications CL-FE6), its dependencies and a size budget. For the size budget I kept the design's S/M class and added a scope budget: the files the task may change and the files it must not change. I set no numeric estimate, because no input gives one. To avoid merge conflicts between parallel tasks, I gave each package's version step to one task and split the test files by task. Both are marked as agent judgement. I took the tier T2 from org.risk_map and checked every task's files against the four areas it names: finance posting, authentication, tenancy and payment execution. The tier is marked pending confirmation by the Developer at the gate. A verifier subagent checked both drafts against the inputs. I then fixed the issues it raised: the version numbers are now labelled as the current versions, the S budget no longer contradicts the version-step assignment, I removed the unsourced 'branch from dev' claim, the 'high-risk areas' framing is now marked as agent judgement, and the QA-oracle claim now cites record:brief.

claims.text: The tier for this feature is T2: the change has no finance posting, authentication, tenancy or payment execution.
Earlier steps carried T2 as an advisory tier, and the design records tenancy, authentication, finance posting and payment execution as not touched.
There are eight stories across four repository lanes (ap_pipeline/DE, ap_forecast/DS, ap_aging/BE, ap_portal/FE), plus an end-to-end story for the Testing Agent.
The design's build tasks DT-1 to DT-7 have size classes M, S, S, S, M, S and M, and all four lanes run in parallel, followed by the Testing Agent's end-to-end proof.
Inside a lane, the delay history depends on the paid_date change, and the CT-1 serialiser depends on the overdue list. The portal depends only on the CT-1 field list.
Feed v3 availability (PQ-6) and the order against PROV-ACME-2026-11 (PQ-5) gate release, not coding.
The CI bar for every lane is compile, unit tests, coverage of at least 90%, static checks, Python 3.9 syntax and lines of at most 140 characters.
The current package versions are ap_pipeline 0.4.0, ap_forecast 0.9.0, ap_aging 1.4.0 and ap_portal 2.3.0 (index.js and package.json).
overdue_with_risk must not call bucket_for, because bucket_for(30) returns '31-60' and would list an invoice that is exactly 30 days past due.
The boundary tests use single-value histories [30], [31], [10] and [11], and the overdue tests use AS_OF = date(2026, 10, 25) with days of 30, 31, 42 and 75.
Money stays Decimal end to end and is a string in JSON and in ap_portal; it is never float, Number() or parseFloat.
No story has a blocking question; every story is ready to build on the interim design, and the [Pending] markers are kept.
Commit messages start with the story ID, and branches are named feature/<story>.
The critic re-check applies to T3 only, so it does not apply to this T2 feature.

open_questions: TKQ-1 (non-blocking): Should tasks carry a numeric estimate in hours or points? No input gives one, so tasks have a size class (S/M) and a scope budget only. Owner: Developer / PM.
TKQ-2 (non-blocking): Confirm the version-step owners (TSK-01, TSK-03, TSK-05, TSK-07) and the test-file split per task. Owner: Developer.
TKQ-3 (non-blocking): Where should the end-to-end harness (TSK-08) live? No input names a location; it stays a test asset that is not deployed. Owner: Testing Agent.
Tier confirmation (non-blocking): T2 comes from org.risk_map and the Design agent concurs, but the Developer must confirm it at the DES-04 gate.

Carried, non-blocking: TQ-1 to TQ-11, DQ-1 to DQ-5, CQ-1 to CQ-4 and CQ-6, SQ-1 to SQ-4, OQ-B1 to OQ-B10, PQ-1 to PQ-6, PQ-P1 to PQ-P7. CQ-5 is answered for this step: the story ID stays the commit prefix and the task ID follows it.
structured.summary: I wrote feat.tasks with eight engineering tasks, one per story. TSK-01 to TSK-07 are the parallel lane tasks for DE, DS, BE and FE, built on the approved design DT-1 to DT-7. TSK-08 is the Testing Agent's end-to-end proof, which runs after the lanes merge. Each task has a goal, components, acceptance criteria and pending markers, tests, dependencies, an S/M size with a file-scope budget, and done-when criteria. I wrote feat.tier as T2: every task was checked against the four areas org.risk_map names, and none touches them. The tier is pending the Developer's confirmation at the gate. There are no blocking questions. A verifier checked both drafts against the inputs and I corrected what it found.

tool_input.command: cd hobasa-design-agent/outputs/FEAT-ZD-48600 && sed -i '' 's/TQ-D\([0-9]\)/TKQ-\1/g' feat.tasks.md && grep -c 'TKQ-' feat.tasks.md
tool_input.description: Rename task open-question IDs to avoid clash with TRD IDs
